title: Invariants of a transported resolution compute locally constant inhomogeneous cohomology
statement:
Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group in universe $u$ and let $r=\max(u,s)$. Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $E:\mathcal A\simeq\operatorname{DiscreteRep}_{\mathbf Z}(G)$ an equivalence [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], and let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}_r$ be invariants after $E$, followed by the underlying additive-group functor. Assume $V$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix $F\in\mathcal A$ and an injective resolution $I$ of $F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $K$ be any cochain complex of abelian groups in universe $r$, with additive equivalences $t_n:K^n\simeq\operatorname{LC}(G^n,E(F))$. Here $\operatorname{LC}$ means functions locally constant in the topological domain, with pointwise addition. Suppose for every $x\in K^n$ and tuple $g=(g_0,\ldots,g_n)$,
$t_{n+1}(d x)(g)=\rho(g_0)t_n(x)(g_1,\ldots,g_n)+\sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^{k+1}t_n(x)(\operatorname{contract}_k(g))$,
where contract multiplies adjacent entries at $k<n$ and drops the last entry at $k=n$. Then for every $q\ge0$ the underlying types of $H^q(V(I^\bullet))$ and $H^q(K)$ are equivalent. No finiteness hypothesis is imposed on the scalar ring or coefficient group.

proof.text: Use the integer invariants infrastructure to install EnoughInjectives on A and finite-limit preservation for invariants after E. This uses the arbitrary-ring functorial embedding theorem and the restricted trivial-action/invariants adjunction, without a finite scalar-ring hypothesis.

Obtain the locally constant complex functor C, its coordinate equivalences, its differential equation and its effaceable delta-functor T, with degree zero naturally isomorphic to V. Apply the effacement criterion to make T universal.

Obtain a universal right-derived delta-functor R for V and identify R in degree zero with V. Extend the degree-zero isomorphism in both directions by universality. Form both composites as delta-functor morphisms; uniqueness of the extension of the identity in degree zero makes both composites identities. This gives a natural isomorphism R^q to T^q. Mathlib InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj computes R^q at F with the supplied resolution I.

The additive coordinates e(F,n) followed by t(n) inverse define termwise isomorphisms C(F)^n to K^n. For each adjacent differential, apply t(n+1), evaluate at a tuple, and use the two inhomogeneous differential equations to prove commutation. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents gives a complex isomorphism. Apply the homology functor and compose with the right-derived comparison and the supplied-resolution isomorphism; take the underlying type equivalence.

theorem nonempty_equiv_invariantResolution_inhomogeneous
    (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
    (A : Type v) [Category.{w} A] [Abelian A]
    (E : A ≌ DiscreteContinuousRep.{0, u, max u s} ℤ G)
    [(E.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ Rep.invariantsFunctor ℤ G ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max u s} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat).Additive]
    (F : A) (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (K : CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{max u s} ℕ)
    (t : ∀ n : ℕ, K.X n ≃+ LocallyConstant (Fin n → G) (E.functor.obj F).obj.V)
    (ht : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : K.X n) (g : Fin (n + 1) → G),
      t (n + 1) ((K.d n (n + 1)) x) g =
        (E.functor.obj F).obj.ρ (g 0) (t n x (fun k ↦ g k.succ)) +
          ∑ k : Fin (n + 1),
            (-1 : ℤ) ^ (k.val + 1) • t n x (Fin.contractNth k (· * ·) g))
    (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (((((E.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ Rep.invariantsFunctor ℤ G ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max u s} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).homology q) ≃ K.homology q)
